--- title: "[Graph.subgraph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract an induced subgraph containing the specified nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25163-L25273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.subgraph(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Induced subgraph](/assets/graphs/subgraph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with node ids 1 to 6; nodes 1, 2, 4, 5 are the ones requested. The induced subgraph keeps those four nodes and every edge among them (1-2, 1-4, 2-5, 4-5), in the accent color; nodes 3 and 6 and their edges are dropped and shown dashed." width="100%"} Returns a new graph containing only the specified nodes and all edges between them (the induced subgraph). This is a direct method that doesn't require prior selection, unlike `transform_to_subgraph_ws()`. An edge is kept only when both of its endpoints are among the requested nodes, so any edge leading out of the chosen set is dropped. Use it to zoom in on a region of a larger network: - analyzing one community, module, or connected component on its own - extracting the neighborhood of a node of interest for closer inspection or plotting - running an expensive algorithm on a manageable piece of a large graph The original graph is not modified. Nodes and edges keep their IDs, so results computed on the subgraph can be matched back to the original by ID. The selection state is not carried over. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs to include in the subgraph. Order does not matter, and repeated IDs are included once. An empty list gives an empty graph. To work from labels, convert them first with `get_id_from_label()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the specified nodes and edges between them. Preserves directedness, weightedness, and node and edge IDs, labels, weights and attributes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any node ID is not found in the graph. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~edge_subgraph`) : Extract specific edges and their endpoints. [](`~transform_to_subgraph_ws`) : Extract the subgraph defined by the current selection. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Taking the three middle nodes of a five-node path keeps the two edges that run between them; the edges to the end nodes are dropped: ::: {#37a94baa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a path: 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) # Get node IDs in path order (get_node_ids() does not guarantee an order) node_ids = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # Extract subgraph of the middle nodes 2, 3, 4 middle_nodes = node_ids[1:4] sub = graph.subgraph(middle_nodes) # Returns 3 sub.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#37a45db2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 sub.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Any three nodes of a complete graph form a triangle, so extracting three nodes from K5 gives a K3 with three edges: ::: {#20fc7bf6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(5) # K5 # Extract K3 subgraph node_ids = list(graph.get_node_ids())[:3] k3 = graph.subgraph(node_ids) # Returns 3 k3.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: IDs, labels, attributes, and weights travel with the nodes and edges: `C` has ID `3` in both graphs. The `A--B` and `B--C` edges are gone because `B` was left out: ::: {#57c68df8 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(weighted=True) g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"], kind="gene") g.add_edges([("A", "B", 1.0), ("B", "C", 2.0), ("C", "D", 3.0), ("A", "C", 4.0)]) ids = [g.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ["A", "C", "D"]] sub = g.subgraph(ids) sub.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['C--D', 'A--C'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#17752f7c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} sub.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
